subject.title: RFC: Per-session tool policies — bridging operator scopes and agent tool access

question: Should Gateway operator scopes become an input to agent tool-policy resolution, and where should that public config/security contract live?
rationale: The code can add a bridge mechanically, but the durable choice is whether operator scopes are a security boundary, how they compose with existing sender/session/binding policies, and what config contract OpenClaw is willing to support.

options.title: Design Scope-Aware Tool Policy
options.body: Approve a typed `toolsByScope` or equivalent contract with documented precedence, enforcement points, tests, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Use Existing Identity Primitives
options.body: Route this need through sender/group policy, binding restrictions, session envelopes, conversation identity, or tenant-RBAC work instead of adding a new scope-keyed config layer.

options.title: Decline Scope-Based RBAC
options.body: Document operator scopes as control-plane access only and recommend separate gateways, trusted proxy identity, or sender policies for multi-user isolation.

recommendation.title: Design Scope-Aware Tool Policy
recommendation.body: Approve a typed `toolsByScope` or equivalent contract with documented precedence, enforcement points, tests, and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent scoped conversation capability work makes this the closest available owner for deciding the policy boundary.
